name_th: ถั่วเน่าแข็บ (ถั่วเน่าแผ่น)
kham_mueang_th: ถั่วเน่าแข็บ
what_it_is_en: Soybeans boiled, fermented 2-3 days with naturally present Bacillus bacteria (in banana-leaf-lined baskets or cloth sacks), ground with salt, pressed into thin rounds and sun-dried on bamboo racks. Keeps for about a year. Associated with Tai Yai (Shan), Tai Lue and Lanna cooking.
flavour_en: Mildly salty, deep umami, fermented aroma that softens when toasted.
used_in: น้ำพริกอ่อง (some recipes)
น้ำพริกถั่วเน่า
where_to_buy_en: Warorot Market (Kad Luang / กาดหลวง): northern food and dry-goods stalls, incl. vendors selling packaged take-home northern items; also at any neighbourhood morning market (กาดเช้า / กาดหมั้ว) or evening market (กาดแลง) (dry-goods / northern ingredient stalls).
substitute_abroad_en: Japanese natto (dried/toasted) or a little Korean doenjang/miso for umami; not identical.

pronunciation.tip_en: Before use, toast the disc over a low flame/charcoal until it lightens and turns crisp-crumbly (reduces the fermented smell), then pound. Tones are Chiang Mai Northern Thai values (24 low-rising, 21 low-falling, 44ʔ high-level glottal, 33 mid, 42 high-falling, 45 high-rising) DERIVED by applying the Chiang Mai tone-box correspondences (Wikipedia 'Northern Thai language') to the etymological Thai spelling. Not checked against a native-speaker recording; treat as a guide.

notes_th: ก่อนใช้ นำถั่วเน่าแข็บมาอังไฟให้สุก สีอ่อนลง กรอบร่วน (ครัว.co)

name_th: ถั่วเน่าเมอะ
kham_mueang_th: ถั่วเน่าเมอะ
what_it_is_en: Ground fermented soybeans mixed with salt, shallot, garlic and dried chilli, wrapped in banana leaf and steamed or grilled.
used_in: eaten as a relish with sticky rice
seasoning in curries and chilli dips
where_to_buy_en: Warorot Market (Kad Luang / กาดหลวง): northern food and dry-goods stalls, incl. vendors selling packaged take-home northern items; any neighbourhood morning market (กาดเช้า / กาดหมั้ว) or evening market (กาดแลง) (sold in banana-leaf packets).
substitute_abroad_en: Miso mixed with a little chilli and garlic (approximation).

pronunciation.tip_en: Tones are Chiang Mai Northern Thai values (24 low-rising, 21 low-falling, 44ʔ high-level glottal, 33 mid, 42 high-falling, 45 high-rising) DERIVED by applying the Chiang Mai tone-box correspondences (Wikipedia 'Northern Thai language') to the etymological Thai spelling. Not checked against a native-speaker recording; treat as a guide.

name_th: ถั่วเน่าซา
kham_mueang_th: ถั่วเน่าซา
what_it_is_en: The first stage after 2-3 days' fermentation: beans with fluffy white mould and a fermented smell; the base for the paste and discs.
flavour_en: Strong fermented aroma, soft beans, mildly salty only after seasoning.
used_in: คั่วถั่วเน่าซา (Tai Yai style stir-fry with galangal, lemongrass, chilli, turmeric, tomato)
where_to_buy_en: any neighbourhood morning market (กาดเช้า / กาดหมั้ว) or evening market (กาดแลง) (less common; ask northern-ingredient vendors).
substitute_abroad_en: Fresh natto.

pronunciation.tip_en: Tones are Chiang Mai Northern Thai values (24 low-rising, 21 low-falling, 44ʔ high-level glottal, 33 mid, 42 high-falling, 45 high-rising) DERIVED by applying the Chiang Mai tone-box correspondences (Wikipedia 'Northern Thai language') to the etymological Thai spelling. Not checked against a native-speaker recording; treat as a guide.

name_th: น้ำปู / น้ำปู๋
what_it_is_en: Rice-field crabs pounded with herbs (lemongrass leaves, turmeric leaves; some places add guava or hog-plum leaves), squeezed and strained, rested overnight, then simmered on low heat for a long time (a day or more) until thick and black. Made once a year in the rainy season, around September-October. Famous in Chiang Rai, Lampang and Nan.
flavour_en: Very intense, earthy, salty-umami, slightly herbal; black and sticky.
used_in: น้ำพริกน้ำปู๋
แกงหน่อไม้
where_to_buy_en: Warorot Market (Kad Luang / กาดหลวง): northern food and dry-goods stalls, incl. vendors selling packaged take-home northern items (northern condiment stalls; sold in small jars). Seasonal fresh batches appear after October.
substitute_abroad_en: No real substitute. A very small amount of Thai shrimp paste (kapi) plus a drop of dark soy gives a distant idea.

pronunciation.tip_en: Northerners write ปู๋ with the ๋ mark because the Chiang Mai tone on ปู sounds rising to Central Thai ears. Tones are Chiang Mai Northern Thai values (24 low-rising, 21 low-falling, 44ʔ high-level glottal, 33 mid, 42 high-falling, 45 high-rising) DERIVED by applying the Chiang Mai tone-box correspondences (Wikipedia 'Northern Thai language') to the etymological Thai spelling. Not checked against a native-speaker recording; treat as a guide.

notes_th: น้ำปูนิยมทำกันในฤดูฝน ช่วงเดือนกันยายน-ตุลาคม ปีหนึ่งทำครั้งเดียว (แม่น้อย)
needs_expert_review: Recipe proportions (3 kg crabs : 6 lemongrass : 2 cups turmeric leaves : 2 Tbsp salt) come from a commercial curry-paste maker's article; confirm with a Nan/Chiang Rai maker.

name_th: ปลาร้า (ปลาฮ้า)
kham_mueang_th: ปลาฮ้า / ฮ้า
what_it_is_en: Salt-fermented fish. Central Thai call it ปลาร้า, Isan ปลาแดก, and in the northern kitchen it is ปลาฮ้า (Northern h for Central r). Some vendors season nam phrik num with it.
used_in: น้ำพริกหนุ่ม (some versions)
น้ำพริกอ่อง (some versions)
where_to_buy_en: Warorot Market (Kad Luang / กาดหลวง): northern food and dry-goods stalls, incl. vendors selling packaged take-home northern items; any neighbourhood morning market (กาดเช้า / กาดหมั้ว) or evening market (กาดแลง). Ask for cooked/boiled (ต้มสุก) fermented fish sauce if eating uncooked.
substitute_abroad_en: Bottled cooked pla ra sauce from Asian groceries; or extra fish sauce + anchovy paste.

pronunciation.tip_en: Northern often drops the l in pl-clusters; forms 'pla' and 'pa' both heard. Tones are Chiang Mai Northern Thai values (24 low-rising, 21 low-falling, 44ʔ high-level glottal, 33 mid, 42 high-falling, 45 high-rising) DERIVED by applying the Chiang Mai tone-box correspondences (Wikipedia 'Northern Thai language') to the etymological Thai spelling. Not checked against a native-speaker recording; treat as a guide.

needs_expert_review: Krua.co only names ปลาฮ้า for the North; exact local production differences from Isan pla daek were not documented in sources opened.

name_th: กะปิ
what_it_is_en: Fermented shrimp paste, used in the CMU Lanna Food nam phrik ong paste and in northern curry pastes; some nam phrik num versions add a little roasted in banana leaf.
used_in: น้ำพริกอ่อง
พริกแกงฮังเล
น้ำพริกหนุ่ม (variant)
where_to_buy_en: Warorot Market (Kad Luang / กาดหลวง): northern food and dry-goods stalls, incl. vendors selling packaged take-home northern items; any market or supermarket.
substitute_abroad_en: Thai/Malaysian shrimp paste (belacan) from Asian groceries.

pronunciation.tip_en: Tones are Chiang Mai Northern Thai values (24 low-rising, 21 low-falling, 44ʔ high-level glottal, 33 mid, 42 high-falling, 45 high-rising) DERIVED by applying the Chiang Mai tone-box correspondences (Wikipedia 'Northern Thai language') to the etymological Thai spelling. Not checked against a native-speaker recording; treat as a guide.

name_th: แคบหมู
name_en: Northern pork cracklings / puffed pork rind
what_it_is_en: 'แคบ' in Northern means animal skin/fat rendered until crisp. Types: ไร้มัน (skin only, no fat), ติดมัน (skin with a fat and meat layer), มันล้วน (all fat), plus แคบไขหมู and buffalo แคบควาย.
flavour_en: Crunchy, porky, salty; ติดมัน is rich, ไร้มัน light and airy.
used_in: eaten with น้ำพริกหนุ่ม and น้ำพริกอ่อง
ขนมจีนน้ำเงี้ยว topping
where_to_buy_en: Warorot Market (Kad Luang / กาดหลวง): northern food and dry-goods stalls, incl. vendors selling packaged take-home northern items: long-running pork-rind shops (Wongnai names Damrong, Je Hong, Sri Phan, Naem Boon Sri); also Ton Phayom market and souvenir shops.
substitute_abroad_en: Chicharrón (Mexican) or UK pork scratchings; pick puffed, not hard, styles.

pronunciation.tip_en: Northern pronounces ค as an unaspirated k. CMU transliterates 'Khaep mu'. Tones are Chiang Mai Northern Thai values (24 low-rising, 21 low-falling, 44ʔ high-level glottal, 33 mid, 42 high-falling, 45 high-rising) DERIVED by applying the Chiang Mai tone-box correspondences (Wikipedia 'Northern Thai language') to the etymological Thai spelling. Not checked against a native-speaker recording; treat as a guide.

name_th: ไส้อั่ว
what_it_is_en: Pork stuffed into pork intestine with a herb paste and grilled. 'อั่ว' means to stuff/insert into the middle; it is traditionally paired with แคบหมู because both came from the same pig slaughter.
flavour_en: Herbal (lemongrass, galangal, kaffir lime), mildly spicy, salty, smoky.
used_in: eaten with sticky rice and น้ำพริกหนุ่ม
where_to_buy_en: Warorot Market (Kad Luang / กาดหลวง): northern food and dry-goods stalls, incl. vendors selling packaged take-home northern items (ready-grilled and vacuum-packed).
substitute_abroad_en: No close substitute; a herby fresh pork sausage grilled over charcoal.

pronunciation.tip_en: Tones are Chiang Mai Northern Thai values (24 low-rising, 21 low-falling, 44ʔ high-level glottal, 33 mid, 42 high-falling, 45 high-rising) DERIVED by applying the Chiang Mai tone-box correspondences (Wikipedia 'Northern Thai language') to the etymological Thai spelling. Not checked against a native-speaker recording; treat as a guide.

name_th: แหนม (จิ๊นส้ม)
what_it_is_en: Pork (with skin) fermented with rice, salt and garlic until sour. Central Thai แหนม; Northern จิ๊นส้ม ('sour meat'); จิ๊นส้มหมก is the version grilled in banana leaf.
used_in: จิ๊นส้มหมก
where_to_buy_en: Warorot Market (Kad Luang / กาดหลวง): northern food and dry-goods stalls, incl. vendors selling packaged take-home northern items (Naem shops).
substitute_abroad_en: Vietnamese nem chua.

pronunciation.tip_en: จิ๊น is the Northern form of ชิ้น 'meat' (ch→j). Tones are Chiang Mai Northern Thai values (24 low-rising, 21 low-falling, 44ʔ high-level glottal, 33 mid, 42 high-falling, 45 high-rising) DERIVED by applying the Chiang Mai tone-box correspondences (Wikipedia 'Northern Thai language') to the etymological Thai spelling. Not checked against a native-speaker recording; treat as a guide.

needs_expert_review: Uncooked fermented pork carries food-safety risks; confirm current guidance.

name_th: หมูสับติดมัน
kham_mueang_th: จิ๊นหมูสับ
what_it_is_en: Minced pork with some fat, the base of nam phrik ong. Chiang Mai News recommends choosing mince with a little fat.
used_in: น้ำพริกอ่อง
where_to_buy_en: Ton Lamyai Market (กาดต้นลำไย), directly opposite Warorot: fresh vegetables, fruit, meat; meat section at Warorot Market (Kad Luang / กาดหลวง): northern food and dry-goods stalls, incl. vendors selling packaged take-home northern items; any market (ask the butcher to mince: สับหื้อแน่).
substitute_abroad_en: Pork mince 15-20% fat.

pronunciation.tip_en: Kham Mueang จิ๊น = meat. Tones not derived for the whole phrase.

needs_expert_review: The Kham Mueang phrase 'จิ๊นหมูสับ' is assembled from จิ๊น (meat) + Central หมูสับ; confirm what vendors actually say.

name_th: พริกหนุ่ม
what_it_is_en: Long, slender, pale yellow-green chilli used green for roasting. Michelin describes it as young unripe chilli; Baan Lae Suan says it is a specific mild variety rather than simply unripe chilli. Not very hot.
flavour_en: Mild to medium heat, sweet-grassy, smoky when charred.
used_in: น้ำพริกหนุ่ม
น้ำพริกน้ำปู๋ (some versions)
where_to_buy_en: Ton Lamyai Market (กาดต้นลำไย), directly opposite Warorot: fresh vegetables, fruit, meat; Muang Mai Market (กาดเมืองใหม่), by the Ping River: wholesale fresh vegetables/fruit from about 2 am, retail stalls through the day; any neighbourhood morning market (กาดเช้า / กาดหมั้ว) or evening market (กาดแลง).
substitute_abroad_en: Anaheim, Hungarian wax, or long green (Turkish/Italian) peppers; mix in a jalapeño if too mild.

pronunciation.tip_en: Northern speakers usually drop the r: 'phik'. หนุ่ม = young (man). Tones are Chiang Mai Northern Thai values (24 low-rising, 21 low-falling, 44ʔ high-level glottal, 33 mid, 42 high-falling, 45 high-rising) DERIVED by applying the Chiang Mai tone-box correspondences (Wikipedia 'Northern Thai language') to the etymological Thai spelling. Not checked against a native-speaker recording; treat as a guide.

needs_expert_review: Sources disagree whether พริกหนุ่ม is a cultivar or just unripe chilli; seed sellers market 'พริกหนุ่มเขียว' as a variety.

name_th: พริกแห้ง (พริกแห้งเม็ดใหญ่ / พริกชี้ฟ้าแห้ง)
what_it_is_en: Dried spur chillies, the base of larb spice mix (CMU uses ½ kg per batch) and of nam phrik ong (small dried bird chillies in CMU recipe).
flavour_en: Hot, smoky when roasted, red colour.
used_in: น้ำพริกอ่อง
พริกแกงฮังเล
น้ำพริกน้ำปู๋ (roasted)
where_to_buy_en: Warorot Market (Kad Luang / กาดหลวง): northern food and dry-goods stalls, incl. vendors selling packaged take-home northern items dry-goods stalls; any market.
substitute_abroad_en: Dried guajillo/puya (milder) or dried Thai chillies from Asian groceries.

pronunciation.tip_en: Tones are Chiang Mai Northern Thai values (24 low-rising, 21 low-falling, 44ʔ high-level glottal, 33 mid, 42 high-falling, 45 high-rising) DERIVED by applying the Chiang Mai tone-box correspondences (Wikipedia 'Northern Thai language') to the etymological Thai spelling. Not checked against a native-speaker recording; treat as a guide.

name_th: พริกขี้หนู / พริกจินดา
kham_mueang_th: พริกขี้หนู
what_it_is_en: Small hot chilli; CMU's nam phrik nam pu uses about 20 fresh bird chillies; the Cookpad version uses red จินดา chillies.
used_in: น้ำพริกน้ำปู๋
น้ำพริกอ่อง (dried)
where_to_buy_en: Ton Lamyai Market (กาดต้นลำไย), directly opposite Warorot: fresh vegetables, fruit, meat; any market.
substitute_abroad_en: Thai bird chillies (fresh or frozen) or other small hot chillies.

pronunciation.tip_en: Tones not derived.

name_th: มะแขว่น
kham_mueang_th: มะแขว่น / มะแข่น / มะข่อง; แม่ฮ่องสอน: หมักข่วง
what_it_is_en: Dried fruit of a thorny tree in the citrus family (Zanthoxylum limonella). Harvested roughly Oct-Dec and sun-dried in bunches. Signature spice of larb spice mix; the eastern Lanna style (Nan, Phrae, Chiang Rai, Phayao, Lampang) of larb mix emphasises it. Young leaves are also eaten raw with chilli dips.
flavour_en: Strong citrus-pine aroma, mild heat and a tongue-tingling numbness Northerners call 'เด้าลิ้น'. Similar to Sichuan pepper.
used_in: น้ำพริกมะแขว่น
where_to_buy_en: Warorot Market (Kad Luang / กาดหลวง): northern food and dry-goods stalls, incl. vendors selling packaged take-home northern items dry-goods / spice stalls (dried pods on stems); highland-produce stalls in season. Renowned sources: Ban Pong Yaeng (Mae Rim), Ngao (Lampang), Nan.
substitute_abroad_en: Sichuan pepper or Nepali timur; use a bit less.

pronunciation.tip_en: Often shortened to 'ma-khwaen' or 'ma-khaen'. Toast briefly then grind. Tones are Chiang Mai Northern Thai values (24 low-rising, 21 low-falling, 44ʔ high-level glottal, 33 mid, 42 high-falling, 45 high-rising) DERIVED by applying the Chiang Mai tone-box correspondences (Wikipedia 'Northern Thai language') to the etymological Thai spelling. Not checked against a native-speaker recording; treat as a guide.

notes_th: รสเผ็ดชา คนเหนือเรียกอาการนี้ว่า 'เด้าลิ้น' (สวพส.)

name_th: มะข่วง
what_it_is_en: A related numbing spice. It is used less than makhwaen: in bamboo-shoot salad with crab paste, bamboo-shoot curry, แกงอ่อม and แกงแค, and rarely in larb mix. Traded in Wang Chin (Phrae) and Li (Lamphun).
used_in: แกงหน่อไม้
where_to_buy_en: Warorot Market (Kad Luang / กาดหลวง): northern food and dry-goods stalls, incl. vendors selling packaged take-home northern items spice stalls (seasonal); ask 'มีมะข่วงก่อ'.
substitute_abroad_en: Sichuan pepper.

pronunciation.tip_en: Tones are Chiang Mai Northern Thai values (24 low-rising, 21 low-falling, 44ʔ high-level glottal, 33 mid, 42 high-falling, 45 high-rising) DERIVED by applying the Chiang Mai tone-box correspondences (Wikipedia 'Northern Thai language') to the etymological Thai spelling. Not checked against a native-speaker recording; treat as a guide.

needs_expert_review: Botanical identity of มะข่วง was not given in the source opened; confirm species.

name_th: ดีปลี
what_it_is_en: Dried long pepper catkins; roasted and pounded into larb spice mix and curry pastes (CMU recipe: 20 pieces; Krua recipe: 7).
where_to_buy_en: Warorot Market (Kad Luang / กาดหลวง): northern food and dry-goods stalls, incl. vendors selling packaged take-home northern items spice stalls; Thai herbal/spice shops.
substitute_abroad_en: Indian long pepper (pippali); or black pepper plus a pinch of cinnamon.

pronunciation.tip_en: Tones are Chiang Mai Northern Thai values (24 low-rising, 21 low-falling, 44ʔ high-level glottal, 33 mid, 42 high-falling, 45 high-rising) DERIVED by applying the Chiang Mai tone-box correspondences (Wikipedia 'Northern Thai language') to the etymological Thai spelling. Not checked against a native-speaker recording; treat as a guide.

name_th: มะแหลบ (เทียนตั๊กแตน)
name_en: Malaep seed (a highland seed spice; Thai trade name เทียนตั๊กแตน)
what_it_is_en: Seed spice grown only above about 600 m in northern mountains; ground seed goes into larb spice mix to cover the smell of meat, notably in frog larb. Also in the traditional Thai 'five tian' medicine group.
flavour_en: Distinctive aroma, bitter and slightly hot.
where_to_buy_en: Warorot Market (Kad Luang / กาดหลวง): northern food and dry-goods stalls, incl. vendors selling packaged take-home northern items spice stalls (small bags); sometimes sold as part of a larb spice set.
substitute_abroad_en: Omit, or use a pinch of dill/caraway seed for aroma (approximation).

pronunciation.tip_en: Tones are Chiang Mai Northern Thai values (24 low-rising, 21 low-falling, 44ʔ high-level glottal, 33 mid, 42 high-falling, 45 high-rising) DERIVED by applying the Chiang Mai tone-box correspondences (Wikipedia 'Northern Thai language') to the etymological Thai spelling. Not checked against a native-speaker recording; treat as a guide.

needs_expert_review: English identity of มะแหลบ is inconsistent across sources (a curry-paste maker describes the plant as a grass; CMU English page lists 'Seeds of Ma laep'; Krua's translated glossary is unreliable). Needs a botanist.

name_th: ลูกผักชี / เม็ดผักชี
kham_mueang_th: ลูกผักชี (Northern: ผักชี = หอมป้อม)
what_it_is_en: Roasted and pounded into larb spice mix (1 Tbsp in Krua's recipe, 2 Tbsp in CMU's).
where_to_buy_en: Warorot Market (Kad Luang / กาดหลวง): northern food and dry-goods stalls, incl. vendors selling packaged take-home northern items spice stalls; any market.
substitute_abroad_en: Coriander seed (same).

pronunciation.tip_en: Tones not derived.

name_th: เครื่องเทศพริกลาบอื่นๆ (ยี่หร่า, โป๊ยกั๊ก, อบเชย, กานพลู, กระวาน, ลูกจันทน์/ดอกจันทน์, เปราะหอม, พริกไทยดำ)
name_en: Other warm spices in Chiang Mai-style larb mix
what_it_is_en: The Chiang Mai-Lamphun style of larb spice mix uses more than ten spices (a sign of wealth and old trade routes): cumin (ยี่หร่า), star anise (โป๊ยกั๊ก), cinnamon (อบเชย), clove (กานพลู), cardamom (กระวาน), nutmeg and mace (ลูกจันทน์/ดอกจันทน์), resurrection lily/aromatic ginger (เปราะหอม) and black pepper.
flavour_en: Warm, aromatic, 'spice-cabinet' depth over the chilli.
where_to_buy_en: Warorot Market (Kad Luang / กาดหลวง): northern food and dry-goods stalls, incl. vendors selling packaged take-home northern items spice stalls.
substitute_abroad_en: Same spices from any supermarket.

pronunciation.tip_en: Tones not derived.

name_th: พริกลาบ (น้ำพริกลาบ / น้ำพริกดำ)
what_it_is_en: Blackish powder/paste of roasted dried chillies and roasted spices (makhwaen, long pepper, coriander seed, cumin, malaep, star anise, cinnamon, clove, cardamom, nutmeg, mace, aromatic ginger, pepper, salt). Used for larb and yam dishes; about 4-5 Tbsp per 1 kg meat (CMU). Families keep their own recipe; the larb master is called สล่าลาบ.
used_in: ยำมะเขือขื่น
where_to_buy_en: Warorot Market (Kad Luang / กาดหลวง): northern food and dry-goods stalls, incl. vendors selling packaged take-home northern items: ready-mixed from spice stalls and northern food shops (ask which town's style: เชียงใหม่ or น่าน).
substitute_abroad_en: Buy a packaged Thai 'larb mueang' spice mix online; Isan larb powder is NOT the same.

pronunciation.tip_en: Tones are Chiang Mai Northern Thai values (24 low-rising, 21 low-falling, 44ʔ high-level glottal, 33 mid, 42 high-falling, 45 high-rising) DERIVED by applying the Chiang Mai tone-box correspondences (Wikipedia 'Northern Thai language') to the etymological Thai spelling. Not checked against a native-speaker recording; treat as a guide.

name_th: ข่า
what_it_is_en: Rhizome used in curry pastes, nam phrik ong (Chiang Mai News version), crab-paste making, Tai Yai soybean stir-fry.
used_in: น้ำพริกอ่อง (some)
พริกแกงฮังเล (ข่าแว่น)
คั่วถั่วเน่าซา
ลาบ (roasted galangal in some styles)
where_to_buy_en: Ton Lamyai Market (กาดต้นลำไย), directly opposite Warorot: fresh vegetables, fruit, meat; any neighbourhood morning market (กาดเช้า / กาดหมั้ว) or evening market (กาดแลง).
substitute_abroad_en: Fresh or frozen galangal; ginger is a weak substitute.

pronunciation.tip_en: Tones are Chiang Mai Northern Thai values (24 low-rising, 21 low-falling, 44ʔ high-level glottal, 33 mid, 42 high-falling, 45 high-rising) DERIVED by applying the Chiang Mai tone-box correspondences (Wikipedia 'Northern Thai language') to the etymological Thai spelling. Not checked against a native-speaker recording; treat as a guide.

name_th: ตะไคร้
what_it_is_en: Stalks and leaves; leaves are pounded with crabs to make nam pu; sliced stalk goes into CMU's nam phrik nam pu.
used_in: น้ำพริกน้ำปู๋
